To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combined therapy consisting of i.p. injections of MMC-treated tumor cell and subsequent and consecutive injections of rIL2 increases antitumour activity against established metastasised melanoma by generating tumour specific CD8+ T lymphocyte in vivo.

the combined therapy with MMC-treated tumor cells (or tumor cell lysates) and rIL-2 induces antitumor activity in vivo against metastatic melanomas by generating tumor-specific cytotoxic CD8+ T lymphocytes.

the combined treatment of an intraperitoneally administered injection of MMC-treated B16 tumor cells and subsequent intraperitoneally injected rIL-2 induced tumor-specific CD8(+) cytolytic T lymphocytes in vivo and that the combined therapy showed significant therapeutic effects against established pulmonary metastasis and subcutaneous tumor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new immunotherapeutic strategy that is based on the induction of antitumour immunity by the combined treatment of MMC-treated tumor cell vaccine and recombinant human IL-2.
the development of new therapeutic modalities for cancer treatment.
the generation of tumor-specific CTL in vivo by combined treatment of tumor cells with MMC and rIL-2, and the therapeutic effect of this treatment against metastatic melanomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combined therapy with MMC-treated tumor cells plus rIL-2 is a promising new therapeutic modality for inducing antitumor activity in vivo.

the combined therapy with MMC-treated tumor cells, followed by rIL-2 administration, is an effective treatment for inducing antitumor immunity, which may be useful for the treatment of metastatic tumors in humans.
the combined therapy with MMC-treated tumor cells plus rIL-2 is a promising therapeutic approach against metastatic melanomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a new method for the induction of tumor-specific CTL in vivo, and that this method is useful in evoking antiviral and antitumor immunity.
we developed a novel immunotherapy that is effective in inducing tumor-specific cytotoxic activity against established metastases in mice.
we have demonstrated that tumor cells can serve as a source of tumor-specific antigens and that the administration of these antigens together with IL-2 can induce tumor-specific CTL in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it’s possible to generate tumor specific T cells from the tumor itself.
the combined treatment of MMC-treated tumor cell vaccine and IL-2 can generate tumor-specific CTL in vivo, which may be effective in treating established metastatic tumors.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using a combination of MMC-treated tumor and rIL-2 to induce antitumor immunity.
